item.title: Live Updates: China’s Xi Warns Trump on Taiwan at Beijing Summit
item.description: Xi Jinping, China’s leader, told President Trump that Taiwan, if handled poorly, could lead to a clash with the United States. The two leaders are also expected to discuss trade and the Iran war at the two-day summit.

item.title: Middle East live: Ship reported seized off UAE coast and bound for Iranian waters
item.description: A ship anchored off the east coast of the United Arab Emirates has been seized and is heading towards Iranian territorial waters, a UK maritime agency said Thursday, without naming the vessel. Lebanon and Israel are to hold new peace talks later in Washington as their latest ceasefire nears its end. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Lebanon’s medics vow to carry on through grief, injuries: ‘These are our people’
item.description: As Israel and Hezbollah exchange fire, dozens of volunteers eat, sleep and pray at a small hospital, waiting to respond to the next airstrike.

item.title: UAE denies Netanyahu secretly visited the country during the Iran war
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu quietly visited the United Arab Emirates during the Israeli-U.S. war with Iran, his office said Wednesday. The UAE later denied any secret visit had occurred.

item.title: Independent Israeli report accuses Hamas of 'systematic' sexual violence during October 7 attacks
item.description: A new independent commission finds Hamas and its allies committed "systematic, widespread" sexual violence during their October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and against hostages they took back to Gaza. This comes as the Knesset passed a law establishing a special military tribunal to try Palestinian militants accused of taking part in the October 7 attacks, under which the death penalty could be handed down. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky tells us more form Jerusalem.

item.title: Iran warns US to accept peace plan or risk collapse of Mideast truce
item.description: Iran’s chief negotiator said on Tuesday that Washington must accept Tehran’s latest peace plan or risk the collapse of the Middle East truce, after President Donald Trump warned the ceasefire was near failure. The war, triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran more than two months ago, has destabilised the region and rattled global markets.
